reuse.why: Most consumers share getPlannedAmount through direct calls or getScheduledAmount, and approximate planning reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, but preview generation shares only range selection.

duplication.why: The main amount decision is centralized, but computeSchedulePreviewTransactions retains its own missing, numeric, and range dispatch.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy belongs in shared/schedules.ts, with API serialization and UI consumers delegating to that layer.

scope.why: The edits stay focused on schedule amount planning, its consumers, the API field, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralization improves ownership, but the preview bypass, loosely typed operator parameters, and outdated policy comments leave competing descriptions and implementations of the rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts: computeSchedulePreviewTransactions calls getRangeAmount while retaining local dispatch instead of delegating the full decision to getPlannedAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: computeSchedulePreviewTransactions replaces midpoint arithmetic with getRangeAmount but preserves the surrounding missing/number/range decision already implemented by getPlannedAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter, getPlannedAmount introduces an isapprox branch, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions bypasses the complete planning helper.
